description: How should parent domain concepts manage their child/subordinate concepts?
question: What is your default approach for parent-child relationship management?

options.name: Parent Manages Directly
options.description: Parent concept has all responsibilities for managing its children (add, remove, find, iterate). Children are accessed through parent.
options.when_to_use: Simple hierarchies, few children, parent naturally owns all child lifecycle operations
options.example: Order has: Get line items, Adds line item, Removes line item, Finds line item by product

options.name: Explicit Collection Class
options.description: Create a named collection class (e.g., Holdings, LineItems) that encapsulates all collection-level operations. Parent delegates to collection.
options.when_to_use: Complex collection logic (filtering, sorting, aggregation), collection behavior is reusable, collection has its own domain meaning
options.example: Portfolio has Holdings. Holdings has: Finds by symbol, Filters by asset class, Calculates total value, Sorts by market value

options.name: Aggregate Root Pattern
options.description: Parent is the aggregate root - all access and modifications to children go through parent. Children cannot be accessed directly from outside.
options.when_to_use: Strong consistency requirements, transactional boundaries, children have no meaning outside parent context
options.example: Order (aggregate root) - LineItems only accessible through Order, never retrieved independently

options.name: Repository Pattern
options.description: Separate repository concept handles persistence and retrieval of parent-child graphs. Domain objects don't manage their own persistence.
options.when_to_use: Clean separation of domain and persistence concerns, complex querying requirements, multiple storage backends
options.example: OrderRepository has: Finds by id, Finds by customer, Saves order (with all line items)
